properties.name: Northampton curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the existing curated visitor boundary using a 300 metre outward and inward buffer. This preserves its deliberate visitor extensions while filling internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces.

project.boundarySource: Curated Northampton visitor boundary with reviewed OSM public green-space extensions
project.researchNotes:
Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The original ONS 2024 built-up area is preserved for provenance; the active visitor boundary closes its internal park and river-corridor gaps without extending beyond Northampton’s outer urban envelope. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon. Bedfordshire and Northamptonshire standalone attraction audit added 2026-08-09. These are explicit Home-only regional destinations and do not alter the host town planner or tourist rating. Northampton visitor-content refresh completed 2026-08-09 after the active visitor boundary was corrected: generic low-value highlights and chain-heavy food entries were replaced with source-backed parks, heritage, nature and independent daytime food stops; repeated OSM picnic tables were consolidated into named locations. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-09: 371 of 416 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown.

Broad visitor-attraction editorial discovery pass 2026-08-13: expanded See discovery beyond historic records using a local OSM extract. Automatically discovered additions remain below Recommended until source-backed editorial review.

touristAppeal.label: Destination draw
touristAppeal.summary: Nationally important architecture, two strong museums, a restored abbey, medieval churches and substantial parkland support a full and varied destination visit.

townGuide.headline: Shoemaking stories, bold architecture and a reinvigorated historic centre
townGuide.intro: Northampton combines Charles Rennie Mackintosh’s 78 Derngate with one of the country’s leading shoe collections, a handsome Guildhall, medieval churches, Delapré Abbey and generous urban parks.
perfectFor: A substantial heritage city with enough variety to justify a dedicated day.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: 78 Derngate, the museum and Delapré Abbey
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start with 78 Derngate and the museum quarter, cross the Market Square and Guildhall, then use Delapré Abbey or Abington Park for a longer afternoon.

townGuide.visitorMood: A substantial heritage city with enough variety to justify a dedicated day.

visitorHighlights.name: 78 Derngate
visitorHighlights.reason: Charles Rennie Mackintosh’s only major English domestic commission is an exceptional architecture and design visit.

visitorHighlights.name: Delapré Abbey
visitorHighlights.reason: A restored historic house and abbey set in extensive parkland, with exhibitions, gardens and a strong daytime food offer.

visitorHighlights.name: Northampton Museum and Art Gallery
visitorHighlights.reason: The internationally important shoe collection and local galleries make this the city’s essential museum.

visitorHighlights.name: Abington Park Museum
visitorHighlights.reason: A compact local-history museum in a 500-year-old manor house, paired naturally with a walk around Abington Park.

visitorHighlights.name: The Holy Sepulchre Church
visitorHighlights.reason: One of England’s few surviving medieval round churches and a distinctive part of Northampton’s skyline.

visitorHighlights.name: Queen Eleanor Cross
visitorHighlights.reason: One of only three surviving Eleanor Crosses, this medieval monument is Northampton's strongest outdoor heritage stop beyond the centre.

visitorHighlights.name: Northampton Guildhall
visitorHighlights.reason: A richly detailed Gothic Revival civic building that gives the centre architectural drama.

visitorHighlights.name: St Peter's Church
visitorHighlights.reason: A nationally important Norman church whose carved stonework rewards a close architectural look.

visitorHighlights.name: Hunsbury Hill Country Park
visitorHighlights.reason: Woodland paths, broad views and the earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort make this the city’s strongest combined green-space and archaeology stop.

visitorHighlights.name: Abington Park
visitorHighlights.reason: Northampton's oldest and most popular park combines lakes, flower displays, a museum, a cafe and traces of a medieval village.

visitorHighlights.name: All Saints Church
visitorHighlights.reason: A prominent rebuilt church and terrace overlooking the Market Square.

visitorHighlights.name: Berserk
visitorHighlights.reason: Berserk is a mapped family attraction within the active Northampton visitor boundary and adds a family-focused visitor experience.

attractionGuide.intro: Berserk is a mapped family attraction within the active Northampton visitor boundary and adds a family-focused visitor experience.

visitorHighlights.name: Boost Trampoline Parks

attractionGuide.headline: Family attraction
attractionGuide.intro: Boost Trampoline Parks is a mapped family attraction within the active Northampton visitor boundary and adds a family-focused visitor experience.

visitorHighlights.name: Northampton Market Square
visitorHighlights.reason: One of England’s largest market squares remains the civic heart of the centre.

visitorHighlights.name: Museum of Leathercraft
visitorHighlights.reason: Museum of Leathercraft is a mapped museum within the active Northampton visitor boundary and adds collections or exhibitions to explore.

attractionGuide.headline: Museum and gallery
attractionGuide.intro: Museum of Leathercraft is a mapped museum within the active Northampton visitor boundary and adds collections or exhibitions to explore.

thingsToDo.name: Look for temporary exhibitions or events

visitorHighlights.name: St Giles' Church
visitorHighlights.reason: A substantial medieval church with a long town-centre story and an attractive churchyard setting.

visitorHighlights.name: The Racecourse
visitorHighlights.reason: A broad historic urban park with tree-lined paths, sports space and room for an easy walk just north of the centre.

visitorHighlights.name: Becket's Park
visitorHighlights.reason: A riverside green beside the marina and university, useful for a quiet pause or a short River Nene walk from the centre.

visitorHighlights.name: Storton's Pits Local Nature Reserve
visitorHighlights.reason: Former gravel workings beside the River Nene now form a meadow, wetland and fen-ditch nature reserve for a quieter local walk.

visitorHighlights.name: Kingsthorpe Meadow Nature Reserve
visitorHighlights.reason: Kingsthorpe Meadow Nature Reserve is a mapped nature reserve within the active Northampton visitor boundary and broadens the visit beyond buildings and historic records.
